data.description: Build the ratified attendee-schedule feature end to end, reproducing the binding prototype one-to-one. Binding artifacts: sequence/attendee-schedule-design.md (decisions + prototype-round rulings) and prototypes/attendee-schedule/index.html (binding visual contract). Scope: (1) single-session Add-to-calendar ICS on /s/:slug reusing src/jobs/calendar/ics.ts; (2) star control as SSR slots + vanilla script module on public agenda cards and session detail (MRQ-120 hooks merged in PR #86; add data-public-session-end); localStorage state; segmented header 'Conference agenda | My schedule (n)'; My Schedule itinerary view with at-a-glance time blocks, NOW line, hover cards, subtle overlap chips, origin-preserving back-nav; (3) D1-backed short codes: POST/GET/PUT /api/v1/public/schedules (code=read, hashed writeKey=write), share URL, open-on-your-phone QR sheet with #k fragment sync, import-as-copy; (4) set-level ICS download + live webcal feed at /api/v1/public/schedules/{code}.ics; (5) Brief-your-agent text block + For-agents doc; overlaps[] in schedule JSON. Register rows 37/38, section T-J (post-eval product feature). Mobile verified at 390px per doc rulings. No login anywhere.
data.title: Attendee personal schedule — star, My Schedule, share/sync, ICS/webcal, agent briefing

data.body: Expert plan written by the design agent (interviewer + prototype author). Design RATIFIED by operator 2026-08-12. Binding: sequence/attendee-schedule-design.md + prototypes/attendee-schedule/index.html. MRQ-120 merged (PR #86) — hooks on main. One PR, five phases, Opus delegator.

Delegator online (agent:delegator-mrq-132). Read the plan, the design doc, and drove the binding prototype in a c11 browser surface end to end: star → My schedule → glance panel with the NOW rule and half-width overlap lanes → overlap chips → phone/share/brief sheets → session detail with origin-preserving back-nav ("← My schedule") and the Google Maps directions link. Worktree ../Marquee-worktrees/mrq-132-attendee-schedule on branch mrq-132-attendee-schedule off github/main (6d8ee25).

Two routing findings from reading the stack before writing code, both verified with a throwaway harness against the repo's own hono/@hono/zod-openapi:

1. A documented path of the shape /api/v1/public/schedules/{code}.ics CANNOT work here. defineApiRoute registers via app.openapi(), which converts {code}.ics to the Hono pattern :code.ics — Hono parses that as a parameter literally named 'code.ics' that matches ANY single segment, so it both shadows the sibling GET /schedules/{code} and fails its own params validation (I measured 400 on both URLs). Same hazard for /api/v1/public/sessions/{slug}.ics against the existing GET /sessions/{slug}. Fix without touching the closed router: put the extension on a static final segment — GET /api/v1/public/schedules/{code}/calendar.ics and GET /api/v1/public/sessions/{slug}/calendar.ics. Unambiguous, fully documented in the OpenAPI doc, still ends in .ics for calendar clients, and webcal:// is the same URL with a different scheme. The only visible consequence is the URL string shown in the share sheet.

2. tests/e2e/ does not exist, and scripts/checks/run-e2e.mjs is a stub that FLIPS to 'requires MARQUEE_E2E_URL or throw' the moment the first spec lands there — a repo-wide switch MRQ-50 owns. I am not flipping it in this ticket. Coverage lands as integration tests in the fast suite plus the in_validation browser-automation gate against a real dev server.

Starting phase 1 (ICS builder + single-session add-to-calendar).

Phase 1 committed (fecd9d1): single-session Add to calendar.

- buildPublishedCalendar() added beside the invite builder in src/jobs/calendar/ics.ts — METHOD:PUBLISH, N VEVENTs, sharing the existing escaping/folding/VTIMEZONE. One builder now serves the single session, the starred set, and the webcal feed, so the three can never describe a session differently.
- New src/lib/public-calendar.ts: LOCATION assembly, stable UIDs (<sessionId>@marquee.stage11.dev), description (speakers + bounded abstract, paragraph breaks preserved), Google/Outlook links, and the Maps directions URL.
- GET /api/v1/public/sessions/{slug}/calendar.ics (anonymous, documented, text/calendar, 404 on unpublished).
- /s/:slug gained the actions row (.ics / Google / Outlook) and a 'Getting there' section whose building name is a real directions link.

One design-adjacent judgement worth recording. The prototype's detail page prints an entrance sentence ('Photo ID required… allow ten minutes for building security'). That string is buildings.access_note, which an existing tested contract (AC-240/252/253, tests/integration/public-site.AC-83-86-240-252-253.test.ts) keeps OFF every public surface — it is speaker-facing operator data, and the venue editor labels it 'shown to speakers'. The ratified ruling for this section is specifically ''Getting there' links to Google Maps directions (building name + address as the destination)', which is exactly what shipped. So the section carries building name → directions link, plus the street address, and no access note; my test now also asserts the note never appears in the anonymous JSON. Flagging as a decision, not asking for one — the ruled behaviour is intact.

npm test: 714 passed, and the two calendar/privacy files pass together. Phase 2 (SSR skeleton: star slots, -end hook, segmented header, containers) next.

Phase 2 committed (bdfc9fa): SSR skeleton + the client core that hydrates it.

Shipped: star in the 40px leading rail on every agenda row and on /s/:slug (SSR aria-pressed=false, script flips it in place); card hook contract extended with data-public-session-end/-title/-room/-speakers; the segmented 'Conference agenda | ★ My schedule (n)' header with a fixed-width count; ?view=mine as a real URL; origin-preserving back-nav with the originating segment staying lit; the sheets and glance/summary containers SSR'd at final size; a noscript line that says where the schedule actually lives.

Two implementation calls:
- view=mine deliberately IGNORES day/track/format/room/q and renders the whole program (the filter bar is hidden in that view, matching the prototype). An itinerary assembled from a filtered agenda would chart and count a fraction of the attendee's picks while calling itself their schedule.
- The view switch is a plain link, not an intercepted pushState. The URL was the point of the ruling (linkable, back-button correct); a SSR navigation here is a single fast render, and it keeps the module small. Everything else in the view — filtering, the glance panel, chips — is client-side with no round trip.

Verified in a real browser against a locally seeded dev worker (vite dev, port 8801, seeded AIE NYC data): star two sessions → header count 2 → localStorage marquee:schedule:aie-ny-2026 holds the ids → My schedule shows exactly those two rows with the empty day group hidden → opening one from there gives '← My schedule' with the mine segment lit and the star already pressed on the detail page.

Note for the validation gate: c11 browser screenshots are erroring in this session ('internal_error: Failed to capture snapshot') on every surface including a fresh one and on /health, so DOM assertions come from c11 eval and pixel evidence will come from Chrome MCP.

Phase 3 next: glance panel with the NOW rule, hover cards, sheets, briefing.

Phase 3 committed (9e9daba): the client module is complete — glance panel (real time axis, half-width lanes for overlapping picks, red NOW rule on the event's clock, NEXT outlined), viewport-clamped hover cards on hover AND focus, quiet overlap chips (touching ≠ overlapping), the three sheets, the agent briefing, and an inline QR encoder.

The QR is worth a note. The sync link carries the private write key in the URL fragment, so the image of it cannot be produced by a server that must never see the key — it has to be drawn client-side. I wrote a byte-mode level-L encoder for versions 1–10 (~200 lines) and it had two bugs that produced perfectly QR-shaped codes that decoded to NOTHING: the format-information strip written transposed (I had (8,i) as row 8 rather than column 8), and alignment patterns skipped wherever their centre crosses a timing line (only bites at v7+). Neither is visible by reading the code or looking at the image. I caught both by rendering the matrices and decoding them with zbarimg and OpenCV's QRCodeDetector; eleven payloads from 5 to 260 bytes across versions 1–10 now decode with both. tests/unit/schedule-qr.MRQ-132.test.ts pins the exact matrix so the next change to the encoder has to redo that verification rather than edit the expectation.

Scope note against the plan's phase list: the client half of the import/sync flow (ensureCode POST, debounced PUT, fragment-key capture with history.replaceState, import-as-copy) landed in this commit rather than phase 4, because splitting one 700-line module across two commits by feature would have made both unreviewable. Phase 4 is now purely server: migration, the schedules API, the feed, and their tests.

Phase 4 next.

Phase 4 committed (7d8b9524): D1 migration + the anonymous schedules API + the live feed.

- migrations/0011_public_schedules.sql (code PK, event_id FK, session_ids JSON, write_key_hash, timestamps). Also added to reset-demo's WIPE_ORDER and DELETE_PLANS — without it a demo reset would leave codes resolving to sessions that no longer exist, and reset-demo.test.ts's table-parity assertion caught exactly that.
- POST /api/v1/public/schedules → 201 {code, writeKey, urls{share,sync,webcal,ics,json}, event, sessions, overlaps}. Code = 'MQ-' + 13 Crockford-ish base32 chars (65 bits, no I/L/O/U so it survives being read aloud); writeKey = 128 bits hex, returned once, stored as SHA-256 only. Session ids accept id OR slug; unpublished ids are a 422 that names them; set capped at 200.
- GET /schedules/{code} → embedded public session objects in time order + computed overlaps pairs. PUT with X-Schedule-Write-Key, constant-time hash compare, scoped to the code's own event so another conference's ids can't repoint it. Empty list is legal (they unstarred everything).
- GET /schedules/{code}/calendar.ics — live feed, webcal:// is the same URL. Unknown code → 404, never an empty VCALENDAR.
- Rate limiting reuses the existing buckets (write for POST/PUT, read for GET), which key anonymous callers by IP. No new limiter, no new state — flagging the choice as the plan asked.

Driven for real against the dev worker, not just in tests: POST returned MQ-ZWNVSQ4CGPQKF with the full urls object and the correct overlap pair for the two clashing seed sessions; the feed served text/calendar with METHOD:PUBLISH and X-WR-CALNAME 'My AI Engineer New York 2026 schedule'; an unknown code 404s; a wrong write key 403s.

Suite: 723 tests green, 41.7s (under the 45s budget). check:api parity clean.

Phase 5 next: the For-agents page, the side-by-side polish pass against the prototype including 390px, then the validation gate and the PR.

VALIDATION — driven against a real running system (vite dev worker on :8801, local D1 seeded with the AIE NYC sample), as the attendee, with headless Chromium at 1440x900 and an iPhone 13 profile at 390px. Evidence attached (transcript, screenshots, the downloaded .ics, the briefing text, the QR PNG lifted off the live canvas).

What I saw work, in order:
- Star three sessions on /agenda including the ruled conflict pair → header count 3, aria-pressed=true, computed background rgb(16,24,32) with the gold glyph. Reload → still 3 (localStorage marquee:schedule:aie-ny-2026).
- Switch to My schedule → h1 'My schedule', '3 sessions Monday 3', exactly 3 rows visible, day header reading '3 starred', slot headers gone.
- Glance panel: blocks classed 'lane-a is-next', 'lane-b', plain — the clashing pair side by side in half-width lanes, the next session outlined. Overlap chips on both members, naming each other.
- Hover a block → the styled card: 'MON, OCT 12 · 09:00 – 09:45', title, room · building, speaker, and the overlap chip.
- Open on your phone → code minted on demand, sync URL with #k=, and a QR drawn on the canvas. I saved the canvas as a PNG and decoded it with zbarimg: it reads back the sync URL character for character.
- Subscribe / share → code, webcal:// URL, share URL. Brief your agent → the paste-ready block with picks inline, overlaps as either/ors, and the live URLs.
- Download .ics → MQ-<code>.ics, a VCALENDAR with METHOD:PUBLISH, X-WR-CALNAME 'My AI Engineer New York 2026 schedule', VTIMEZONE, and 3 VEVENTs.
- Open a session from the itinerary → '← My schedule', the mine segment still lit, the star already pressed, and the .ics/Google/Outlook row plus a Google Maps directions link.
- /agenda/agents renders the full loop for a machine reader.
- Second device on the SHARE link: banner 'Someone shared a schedule with you — 3 sessions', count 0 → 3 after import, and that device did NOT adopt the code (their stars stay theirs).
- Phone on the SYNC link: fragment stripped from the address bar by replaceState, code AND write key adopted, count 3. Unstarring one session on the phone pushed through — GET /schedules/{code} on the server then held 2 sessions, without the phone ever having created a code of its own. Cross-device sync proven end to end.
- 390px: brand row + full-width two-segment switch, star rail intact, 2-up export row. Zero horizontal overflow at 375, 390 and 768 on /agenda, /agenda?view=mine, /s/:slug and /agenda/agents.
- Zero page errors and zero console errors across the whole run.

Two real defects the drive caught and I fixed: a pasted URL in a seeded abstract was wider than the phone column and dragged the page sideways (card prose now breaks, not the layout), and the mobile view switch wrapped 'My schedule' onto two lines so one control read as two.

One false alarm worth recording so nobody re-chases it: in the c11 embedded browser the starred stars painted white with a black glyph. It was not a CSS or ARIA bug — the pane's animation timers were throttled, so the 110ms background transition never advanced. With transition:none the ink background applied instantly, and in Chromium the same element computes rgb(16,24,32) on the first frame. I briefly 'fixed' it by moving the styling to a class and then reverted that once I had the real cause; the aria-pressed selectors from the prototype are what shipped.

npm run pr-gate --ticket=MRQ-132: PASS in 32.5s (budget 120s) — three typechecks, production build, shell truth, design contract, API contract, route map, the 45s fast suite, and the merged AC trace.

data.reason: Auto code-review returned FAIL (implementation-level): 4 MAJOR findings. Fixing on the same branch/PR.

provenance.reason: Auto code-review returned FAIL (implementation-level): 4 MAJOR findings. Fixing on the same branch/PR.

data.body:
Code review (art_01KZVETWY0KM70NTNJQP1HVTC9) returned FAIL with 4 MAJOR + 8 MINOR findings. Every one was real. All fixed in 133eea5e on the same branch/PR, and each fix proven in a browser rather than argued:

MAJOR — a pulled talk broke every export path permanently. Fixed: the 422 now carries error.details.unknownSessionIds and the client drops exactly those and retries once. Measured: a schedule carrying a bogus id opened the share sheet with a real code, pruned the stale id from localStorage, and the header count went 4 → 3 with no error shown.
MAJOR — the feed could diverge silently forever (fire-and-forget PUT that only caught rejected promises). Fixed: response checked, unlanded pushes remembered, re-sent on visibilitychange/online. Measured with an aborted PUT: device 2 / server 3 while 'offline', server 2 within two seconds of the tab returning.
MAJOR — '★ My schedule (n)' rendered a hard 0 on /speakers, /p/:slug and /agenda/agents. Fixed: those shells carry the schedule config and the script. Measured: 3, 3, 3.
MAJOR — the rate limit was declarative only (no limiter adapter exists in this repo; every route gets allowAllRateLimiter). Fixed for this endpoint specifically with a local KV fixed window, 30 creations per hour per IP, keyed on cf-connecting-ip, with unit coverage including 'a missing KV binding means no ceiling, not a refused service'. The repo-wide limiter gap is not mine to close; the PR now says so plainly.

MINORs fixed: in-flight toggles now reach the code (proven with a delayed POST — server holds 3); the NOW rule and Next chip tick every 60s and on tab return; failSheet writes to its own error slot instead of eating the sheet's copy; sheets trap Tab and restore focus to their opener (proven: focus stayed inside, then returned to the 'share' button); a midnight-crossing session measures its end forward from its start; a sync link that binds two devices now announces itself instead of adopting in silence. The e2e gap and the whole-programme load on ?view=mine were already recorded decisions in the PR body — the reviewer's ask on both was 'state it explicitly', which the PR does.

Regression: the full attendee flow re-driven end to end after the fixes — star → itinerary → glance/lanes/chips → phone QR → share → briefing → .ics → back-nav → friend import → phone sync → unstar propagating to the shared code. All green, zero page errors (the single console 422 is the deliberate stale-star probe).

npm test 729 passed. pr-gate PASS in 45.2s. One earlier gate run reported over-budget on the fast suite at 49.2s with 729 passing and load average 25 on a 16-core box; re-run clean at 32.6s, so it was contention, not a defect — flagging it because the budget is an objective, not an oracle.

MRQ-132 shipped as PR #102 (https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/marquee/pull/102), six commits on mrq-132-attendee-schedule off github/main@6d8ee25. NOT deployed — merging does not ship (DEPLOY.md), and nobody asked for a deploy.

WHAT SHIPPED, against the ratified prototype
- Star in a fixed 40px leading rail on every agenda row and on /s/:slug; gold-on-ink starred, quiet outline unstarred, 110ms pulse. SSR ships it state-unknown; the module flips it in a slot that already exists.
- Header segments 'Conference agenda | ★ My schedule (n)' on every public page, count in a 22px fixed slot.
- /agenda?view=mine as a real URL: at-a-glance panel (three day columns on a real axis, overlapping picks in half-width lanes, red NOW rule on the event clock, NEXT outlined), viewport-clamped hover cards on hover and focus, quiet overlap chips, the export row, and honest empty states. The itinerary deliberately renders the WHOLE programme and ignores facets — an itinerary built from a filtered agenda would count a fraction of the attendee's picks and call it their schedule.
- Origin-preserving back-nav with the originating segment still lit.
- /s/:slug: star + Add to calendar (.ics/Google/Outlook) + 'Getting there' as a real Google Maps directions link.
- D1 public_schedules + POST/GET/PUT /api/v1/public/schedules and the live feed. Read is the code; write is the key (returned once, stored as SHA-256, constant-time compared, scoped to the code's own event). Share link, sync link with the key in the fragment, import-as-copy, and a QR drawn client-side because the key must never reach a server.
- /agenda/agents: the For-agents doc as a fetchable page rather than the prototype's modal, since its entire audience is machines.

DECISIONS A REVIEWER SHOULD KNOW
1. The feed is /schedules/{code}/calendar.ics, not /schedules/{code}.ics. A documented '{code}.ics' registers as the Hono pattern ':code.ics' — a parameter literally named 'code.ics' matching any segment — which shadows the sibling JSON route and 400s both URLs. Measured before writing the route. Same for /sessions/{slug}/calendar.ics.
2. The prototype's entrance sentence is buildings.access_note, which AC-240/252/253 keeps off public surfaces. The ruled behaviour ('Getting there links to Maps, building + address as destination') shipped intact; a test asserts the note stays out of the anonymous JSON too.
3. No tests/e2e specs: that directory is a repo-wide switch (first spec flips npm run e2e from stub to 'requires MARQUEE_E2E_URL or throw') that MRQ-50 owns. Coverage is integration tests plus the browser validation gate.
4. Rate limiting: the framework's rateLimit policy is vocabulary only — no limiter adapter exists in this repo, every route gets allowAllRateLimiter. Rather than leave the one endpoint that writes durable rows for an anonymous caller unbounded, creation carries a local KV fixed window (30/hour/IP). The repo-wide gap is unchanged and is called out in the PR.

THE INDEPENDENT REVIEW, AND WHAT IT CAUGHT
The auto code-review returned FAIL with four majors, all real, all fixed in 133eea5e and each proven in a browser: a pulled talk permanently broke every export path (422 now names unknownSessionIds; the client prunes and retries — verified 4 → 3 with a working share sheet); the debounced PUT swallowed non-ok responses so the feed could go stale forever (now checked, remembered, re-sent on visibilitychange/online — verified device 2 / server 3 offline → server 2 on return); the count read a hard 0 on /speakers, /p/:slug and /agenda/agents (now 3, 3, 3); and the inert rate limit above. Eight minors also fixed: in-flight toggles reaching the code, a ticking NOW rule, an error slot that does not eat the sheet's copy, Tab trapping and focus restore, midnight-crossing geometry, and a sync link that announces itself instead of adopting in silence.

Two re-runs of the review after the fixes both TIMED OUT at the harness's 600s cap without producing an artifact — the diff is ~2,900 lines. That is a harness limit, not a verdict; I stopped re-firing rather than burn 10 minutes a try. A second pass is worth running if the orchestrator wants one.

VALIDATION (evidence attached: transcript, 14 screenshots, the downloaded .ics, the briefing, the QR PNG, and the three harnesses)
Driven end to end against a real dev worker with seeded data, Chromium 1440x900 and an iPhone 13 profile at 390px: star → count → reload → itinerary → glance/lanes/chips/hover → phone QR → share → briefing → .ics → back-nav → for-agents → a friend importing a copy → a phone adopting the sync link and pushing an unstar through to the shared code. Zero page errors. Zero horizontal overflow at 375/390/768 on all four public surfaces. The QR lifted off the live canvas decodes back to the exact sync URL with zbarimg.

The QR encoder is worth one line of institutional memory: it had two bugs that produced perfectly QR-shaped codes decoding to NOTHING (a transposed format-information strip; alignment patterns skipped where they cross a timing line, which only bites at v7+). Neither is visible by reading the code or looking at the image — both were caught by decoding the output with zbarimg and OpenCV. A golden-matrix unit test pins it so the next change has to redo that verification.

Also chased and dismissed: starred stars painting white in the c11 embedded browser. Not a CSS or ARIA bug — the pane's animation timers were throttled so the 110ms background transition never advanced. I briefly 'fixed' it by moving the paint to a class, then reverted once I had the real cause; the prototype's aria-pressed selectors are what shipped.

GATE: npm test 729 passed; npm run pr-gate --ticket=MRQ-132 PASS (45.2s of a 120s budget). One earlier gate run tripped the 45s suite objective at 49.2s with 729 green and load average 25 on 16 cores; a clean re-run came in at 32.6s.

LEFT UNDONE, deliberately: no deploy; no e2e specs (see 3); no retention sweep for schedule rows — nothing deletes them outside a demo reset, which is worth a follow-up ticket. The worktree still holds three untracked drive*.review.mjs scratch files written by the review agent into my worktree; they are not mine to delete and are not in any commit.

Merge confirmed — nothing left for me to do here. PR #102 was already merged before this instruction reached me: merge commit 8098c380a472ab99751ca8cf638c4f15cc60f427, merged by Atin (BenevolentFutures) at 2026-08-12T18:07:48Z. The remote branch has been deleted.

Verified on github/main rather than assumed: the review-fix content is present (unknownSessionIds in both the route and the client module; checkScheduleCreateLimit in src/lib/public-schedules.ts and the routes file), and a file-by-file diff of every MRQ-132 file between main and my branch tip shows main is a strict superset — the only differences are later work (#111 MRQ-133 and #112's speaker-directory search) touching public-agenda.route.tsx and PublicAgendaPage.tsx. No MRQ-132 content was dropped in any reconciliation.

Main has since moved five commits past the merge (#110, #107, #99, #112, #111, #113). Still not deployed — merging does not ship.

Left standing, not mine to remove without a word: the worktree ../Marquee-worktrees/mrq-132-attendee-schedule, whose tip 30321fc1 is a 'merge main into MRQ-132' commit authored by someone else, and three untracked drive*.review.mjs scratch files the review agent wrote into it.
